facts.raw_span: A 62-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis
treated with fingolimod for 3 years
tender nodule on her forehead, which had gradually grown over 3 weeks
bumping her forehead on an air-conditioning unit several months prior
denied fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia
Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
No other lesions on full-body skin examination
White blood cell count: 3.9/μL
Lymphocyte count: 0.65/μL
Skin biopsy: Granulomatous inflammation composed of histiocytes, giant cells, and lymphocytes admixed with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules
Tissue culture: Grew Cryptococcus neoformans
HIV test: Negative

concepts.why: The patient has a tender nodule on her forehead with granulomatous inflammation and narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules on skin biopsy, which is consistent with cutaneous cryptococcosis.
The patient is being treated with fingolimod, which is known to cause immunosuppression, and has a low lymphocyte count, indicating impaired immune function.
The patient has a history of multiple sclerosis, which is a chronic neurological disorder.
The patient has a low lymphocyte count and a history of immunosuppression, which suggests a deficiency in cell-mediated immunity.
The patient has a history of immunosuppression and has developed a cutaneous cryptococcal infection, which is an opportunistic infection.
The patient has a skin biopsy showing granulomatous inflammation and narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules, which is consistent with a fungal infection.
The patient has a history of immunosuppression and has developed a cutaneous cryptococcal infection, which may be related to immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS).
The patient has a history of immunosuppression and has developed a cutaneous infection, which may be related to chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis (CMC).

rationales.F01: Multiple sclerosis is a known condition that may increase the risk of certain infections, but it is not directly related to the current symptoms.
rationales.F02: Fingolimod is an immunosuppressive medication that can increase the risk of opportunistic infections, including cutaneous cryptococcosis.
rationales.F06: The presence of an eroded, crusted papule on the forehead is a characteristic skin lesion of cutaneous cryptococcosis.
rationales.F10: The skin biopsy showing granulomatous inflammation and narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules is diagnostic of cutaneous cryptococcosis.
rationales.F11: The growth of Cryptococcus neoformans in tissue culture confirms the diagnosis of cutaneous cryptococcosis.
rationales.F12: The negative HIV test result rules out HIV infection as a cause of immunosuppression, but does not rule out other causes of immunosuppression, such as fingolimod therapy.
